subject: Scan drift detected — re-run, remediation windows, and attestation
messages:
From: BrightScan Security <alerts@brightscan.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Auditor Team <auditor@finserve.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: [ACTION] Scan configuration drift detected for FinServe - partial coverage

Hi Ben,

We observed a configuration drift in the FinServe scan profile tied to your account. During the weekly scheduled run today we detected that a subset of IP ranges (10.24.96.0/22) were excluded due to an outdated inclusion list, resulting in ~18% of hosts not being scanned.

What we did: reconfigured the target list, re-ran discovery in a dry-run, and generated a delta report attached: scan-drift-summary-20260130.csv (CSV).

Preliminary impact: 7 medium and 2 high CVE exposures were surfaced across the missed hosts (details in the CSV). We recommend an immediate authenticated re-scan and triage.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm authorization to perform authenticated re-scan (we have creds from the onboarding vault)
- If approved, we will re-run within 24 hours and provide a findings PDF and remediation suggestions
- Otherwise we can provide a scoped report for your team to pull and re-run locally

We flagged this as priority P1 due to the missed coverage and will hold the re-run pending your confirmation.

Regards,
Morgan Lee
BrightScan Security
[Attachment: scan-drift-summary-20260130.csv (csv)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: BrightScan Security <alerts@brightscan.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Auditor Team <auditor@finserve.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Scan configuration drift detected for FinServe - partial coverage

Thanks Morgan — and thanks for the quick catch.

Confirming: authorize BrightScan to proceed with the authenticated re-scan immediately. Use the vault creds tagged finserve/production-scan. Please prioritize high/critical exposures and include full evidence (proof of scan timestamps, host lists, and exportable CSV/PDF).

Kimberly/Marissa: looping you in for visibility and to coordinate any compensating controls if the re-run surfaces anything exploitable.

Requests for the run:
- Target re-scan within 24 hours
- Export findings in both CSV and PDF (include exploitability notes and recommended fix owners)
- If any CVE has a public exploit, please flag and call it out separately

Ben
Ben Carter | Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightScan Security <alerts@brightscan.com>, Auditor Team <auditor@finserve.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Scan configuration drift — internal plan and SLA commitments

Ben — thanks. Quick internal plan to keep this audit-friendly and to meet our SOC2 commitments:

1) Operations (Marissa) to approve emergency authenticated re-scan and monitor for noisy traffic 
2) Infra to apply temporary WAF rule to reduce exposure window for any remotely exploitable findings (Marissa, please confirm)
3) Triage: Security will take ownership of high/critical findings and map to owners in the service teams
4) Timeline: BrightScan to re-run within 24 hours; initial remediation plan due EOD +48h; closure expected within 14 days for non-exploited medium items, expedited 72-96h for high/critical where possible
5) Evidence: we will produce an attestation letter and attach export logs (scan hashes, timestamps, host lists) for FinServe and for SOC2 evidence.

I created a ticket for tracking: SEC-842 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-842). Marissa — please confirm the compensating control and the Ops go-ahead.

Kim
Kimberly Park | Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
[Signature]

From: BrightScan Security <alerts@brightscan.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Auditor Team <auditor@finserve.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Feb 2026 11:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Re-run complete — findings and remediation windows (SEC-842)

Hi all,

Re-run completed at 2026-02-01T10:22:00-08:00. Attached: re-run-findings-20260201.pdf (summary) and a CSV export of the closed/open items. Highlights:
- 2 High: CVE-2025-3387 (public exploit, assigned to web-team), CVE-2024-9012 (privilege escalation, patched upstream)
- 5 Medium: various outdated libs with recommended upgrade paths
- All previously unscanned hosts were included and verified (host list attached)

Action items and windows:
- Web-team to prioritize CVE-2025-3387 with hotfix within 72 hours (target 2026-02-04 17:00 PST)
- Ops to schedule patching for medium items during the 14-day maintenance window
- We exported scan evidence and signed hashes: re-run-findings-20260201.pdf; cve-closure-log-20260203.csv will reflect final states after remediation

Let us know if you require a signed attestation for your auditor; we can provide a scanned statement with timestamps and run hashes.

Regards,
Morgan Lee
BrightScan Security
[Attachments: re-run-findings-20260201.pdf, hostlist-20260201.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: BrightScan Security <alerts@brightscan.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Auditor Team <auditor@finserve.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: FINAL: Remediation attestation and evidence handoff (SEC-842)

Team and Auditor —

Following the BrightScan re-run and internal remediation work:
- CVE-2025-3387: hotfix deployed to production 2026-02-03T10:55:00-08:00 (rollback tested; no service impact).
- CVE-2024-9012: patch applied to all affected hosts 2026-02-03T12:30:00-08:00.
- All medium items scheduled and tracked in SEC-842; closure target for non-critical items set for 2026-02-17.

Attached is the closure CSV (cve-closure-log-20260203.csv) with per-host evidence, patch IDs, and scan hashes. For SOC 2 evidence purposes, we confirm the following:
- Scan cadence: weekly scheduled authenticated scans (nightly discovery, weekly vulnerability scan)
- Exception handling: deviations are logged to SEC-842; compensating controls were applied (WAF rule) and removed after closure; change approvals recorded in Ops change log
- SLA commitment: Redwood commits to notifying customers within 24 hours of any scan coverage gaps and to provide remediation evidence within 14 days for non-exploited mediums and expedited handling for high/critical CVEs as documented above.

If FinServe requires a signed attestation PDF for their auditor, we will produce one and route via DocuSign by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — and please file any follow-ups into SEC-842.

Ben Carter | Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cve-closure-log-20260203.csv (csv)]
